evals.prompt: Build a small React synth: one oscillator through a lowpass filter and a gain. The UI has a volume slider, a cutoff slider, and a 'Sweep' button that ramps the cutoff from its current value up to 12 kHz and back over 2 seconds. Use @audiorective/core and @audiorective/react. Write the audio class, the engine module, and the React components as separate files. Don't run anything.
evals.expected_output: A Synth AudioProcessor subclass owning the nodes, an engine module using createEngine, and React components that read params with useValue and call a sweep method
expectations: Defines a class that extends AudioProcessor from @audiorective/core
Constructs the audio nodes as local variables before calling super() and binds params to AudioParams via bind
Exposes a getter named output on the processor
The filter sweep (setValueAtTime / linearRampToValueAtTime against currentTime) is implemented as a method on the processor class, not inside a React component or hook
The React button handler only calls the processor method (no scheduling code in the component)
Uses useValue to read a param in a React component and writes back with param.value = ...
Creates the engine with createEngine and exposes EngineProvider/useEngine via createEngineContext
Does not import or use Tone.js
Does not use a separate state store (Redux, Zustand, React useState) to mirror audio parameter values

evals.prompt: We're adding an audio workspace to a Next.js 15 app (app router). The engine module is at app/studio/audio/engine.ts and exports `engine` created with createEngine from @audiorective/core. Right now `next build` fails with EngineEnvironmentError. Show me the file layout and code changes that fix this properly. Don't run anything.
evals.expected_output: A client-only boundary (next/dynamic with ssr: false) around the audio subtree, with the engine module only imported from inside it
expectations: Uses next/dynamic with ssr: false (or an equivalent client-only boundary) to mount the audio subtree
Keeps createEngine at module scope inside the client-only subtree rather than making it lazy or nullable
Explains that 'use client' alone does not prevent server evaluation
Does not recommend a typeof window guard, a nullable engine, or a lazy getter as the fix
Identifies that the fix is to move the import path that reaches the engine module inside the boundary

evals.prompt: Write a 16-step drum machine (kick, snare, hat) in TypeScript with @audiorective/core and @audiorective/clock. It needs start/stop, a BPM control, and toggling steps while it's playing. Samples are at /kit/kick.wav, /kit/snare.wav, /kit/hat.wav. Vanilla TS with a minimal DOM UI is fine. Don't run anything.
evals.expected_output: A DrumMachine processor that uses the clock's look-ahead tick windows to schedule Sampler triggers, with the step pattern in a Cell and the UI only toggling and reading state
expectations: Uses @audiorective/clock for transport and tempo rather than setInterval or a hand-rolled scheduler
Uses Sampler (or another audiorective playback primitive) for the one-shot drum hits
Stores the step pattern as a Cell (or in a plain class holding a Cell), not as a Param<boolean[][]> and not in DOM state
Schedules hits from the clock's tick windows / rulers with audio-time timestamps, not on the main thread at playback time
Keeps scheduling logic in the audio class; DOM handlers only call methods like toggleStep / start / stop
Resumes or starts the AudioContext from a user gesture

evals.prompt: In our audiorective project, calling `sampler.params.mute.value = true` throws 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading value)'. The docs you have say Sampler has a mute param. What's going on and what should I do?
evals.expected_output: Diagnoses a version mismatch between the installed @audiorective/core and the documented API, checks the changelog and the installed version, and recommends upgrading
expectations: Suspects the installed package predates the documented API rather than assuming the docs are wrong
Consults the changelog reference to find which version added Sampler.params.mute
Checks the installed version via node_modules/@audiorective/core/package.json or an equivalent command
Recommends upgrading the @audiorective/* packages together instead of hand-rolling a mute gain node
